'''Sydney Goldstein''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal|last1 = Lighthill|first1 = J.|authorlink = James Lighthill|doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1990.0029|doi-access = free|title = Sydney Goldstein. 3 December 1903-22 January 1989|journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|volume = 36|pages = 174|year = 1990}}</ref> (3 December 1903 – 22 January 1989) was a [[Great Britain|British]] [[mathematician]] noted for his contribution to [[fluid dynamics]].<ref name="mact">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Goldstein}}</ref><ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy |id=18554}}</ref> He is described as: "... one of those who most influenced progress in fluid dynamics during the 20th century."<ref name="frs"/>

He was especially known for his work on steady-flow laminar boundary-layer equations and  on the turbulent resistance to rotation of a disk in a fluid. Goldstein was extremely knowledgeable on [[aerodynamics]] and his work had a significant impact in that area.<ref name="mact"/>

==Early life==
Goldstein was born into the [[History of the Jews in Kingston upon Hull|Jewish community of Hull]], where his family ran a furniture store.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hull, England|url=https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/hull|access-date=2021-08-08|website=www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org|language=en}}</ref> After his mother died he moved to live with an aunt and attended Bede Collegiate School in [[Sunderland, Tyne and Wear|Sunderland]].<ref name=WwW>SYDNEY GOLDSTEIN, Who was Who, A&C Black</ref> At the [[University of Leeds]] in 1921 he studied mathematics, but was to move to [[St John's College, Cambridge|St John's College]], [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]], graduating from the [[Mathematical Tripos]] in 1925 and gaining the [[Smith's Prize]] in 1927. He was awarded an Isaac Newton Studentship to continue research in applied mathematics under [[Harold Jeffreys]]. His 1928 PhD thesis was entitled ''The Theory And Application Of [[Mathieu function|Mathieu Functions]]''.<ref name="mathgene"/>

==Career==
He was appointed Rockefeller Research Fellow and spent a year working in [[University of Göttingen]].<ref name="mact"/> In 1929 he became a  fellow of St John's College but later the same year was appointed to a lectureship in Mathematics at the [[School of Mathematics, University of Manchester|University of Manchester]]. At Manchester the influence of [[Osborne Reynolds]] and [[Horace Lamb]] in fluid dynamics was still felt there and had a strong effect on Goldstein.<ref name="mact"/> Moving to Cambridge in 1931 he took over the editorship of ''Modern Developments in Fluid Dynamics'' on Lamb's death.

During [[World War II]] Goldstein worked on boundary layer theory at the [[National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom)|National Physical Laboratory]] and at the end of the war he was appointed to the [[Beyer Chair of Applied Mathematics]] in Manchester. He was elected to the membership of [[Manchester Literary and Philosophical Society]]  in 1947.<ref>Memoirs And Proceedings Of The Manchester Literary And Philosophical Society Vol-46-47 (1947)</ref>

Goldstein strongly supported the [[State of Israel]] and in 1950 he accepted the chairmanship of the department of mathematics at [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]]. Having made a major contribution to the establishment of the Technion, he found the administrative load too heavy<ref name = "mact"/> and moved again, accepting the chair of  Gordon McKay Professor of Applied Mathematics at [[Harvard University]] in 1954.<ref name=WwW /> He retired in 1968 but continued as an emeritus professor at Harvard.

==Honours==
*[[Mayhew Prize]], 1925
*[[Smith's Prize]], 1927
*[[Adams Prize]], 1935
*[[Fellow of the Royal Society]], 1937<ref name="frs"/>
*Worked at the Aerodynamics Division, [[National Physical Laboratory, UK|National Physical Laboratory]], 1939–45
*Chairman, [[Aeronautical Research Council]], 1946–49
*Foreign Member, Royal Netherlands Academy of Sciences and Letters (Section for Sciences), 1950
*Plenary Speaker, [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], 1954<ref>{{cite book|author=Goldstein, S.|chapter=On some methods of approximation in fluid mechanics|volume=1|pages=277–298|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Amsterdam, September 2–September 9, 1954|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1954.1/Main/icm1954.1.0277.0298.ocr.pdf}}</ref>
*[[Timoshenko Medal]], 1965
*Foreign Member, Finnish Scientific Society (Section for maths and physics), 1975

==Selected publications==
* ''Modern Developments in Fluid Dynamics'', 1938. (Editor)
* ''Lectures on Fluid Mechanics'', 1960.
